state: The deposit from our Hartwell Hall booking still hasn't come back, and I know your team's been swamped with the year-end filings. If you get a spare moment this week to check on it, I'd be glad to send over the original invoice number again — whatever makes it easier to track down on your end.

I'm so sorry to bother you again about this, Priya, but would you possibly have a moment to resend the onboarding checklist? I'd be endlessly grateful and promise not to make a habit of pestering you.
Shocking, I know, but I still don't have the final spec doc — could you send it over when you get a chance?
Apparently I'm becoming best friends with your ticketing system — could you please add me to the Atlas dashboard? Thanks a lot!

Dear Mr. Ibarra, I'm so sorry to impose on your very busy schedule, but I would be immensely grateful if you could spare a few minutes to share your thoughts on the draft proposal I sent last week. Please don't hesitate to tell me if now isn't a good time — I completely understand. Thank you so very much for considering this; your feedback means the world to me.

Need you in the conference room at 3pm Thursday to go over the Q3 budget numbers. Bring the vendor contracts and the revised timeline. We're behind schedule so don't plan on this running short. I'll send the room number once it's booked.

Hi Daniel, I finished reading through the marketing draft you sent over. Could you let me know your thoughts on the pricing section by Friday? I want to make sure we're aligned before the client call next week. Let me know if you need more time.

Hi Ms. Alvarado, I hope your week is going well. I'm writing to ask if it might be possible to extend the deadline for the Hendricks report by three days — a family matter has taken more time than expected. I'd really appreciate the extra time, and please let me know if that works on your end. Thank you so much for understanding.
I'm terribly sorry to add to your plate, but whenever you have a free moment, would you mind granting me access to the shared drive? I'd be endlessly grateful for your help.

Dear Professor Whitfield,

I hope this message finds you well and that the semester has been treating you kindly. I am writing with a rather large request, and I want to say upfront how sorry I am to even ask given how full your calendar must already be.

Would it be at all possible to schedule a short meeting sometime in the next two weeks to discuss my thesis proposal? I know your time is extraordinarily valuable, and I promise to keep the conversation as brief and focused as you need it to be. I am happy to work entirely around your schedule, including early mornings, evenings, or even a quick call if that would be easier than finding room on your calendar.

I want to say how deeply grateful I already am for the guidance you've given me this term — it has made an enormous difference, and I would not presume to ask for more of your time if I did not think it truly mattered for the project. If a meeting simply isn't feasible right now, please don't feel any obligation; I would be just as thankful for a few written thoughts whenever it's convenient.

Thank you so much, again, for everything. I know how fortunate I am to have your support, and I will happily adjust to whatever works best for you.

With sincere gratitude and respect,
Marcus Devereaux
I already told you the meeting is at 9, not 9:30 — figure out your calendar before you waste everyone else's time.

No rush at all — it's only been sitting broken for two weeks, so what's one more day, right? Take your time getting the Hartley file corrected; I'm sure whenever you circle back to it will be fine for everyone waiting on it downstream.

In all seriousness, here's what I actually need. The client ID on the Hartley contract was entered wrong back in March, and it has thrown off three separate reports since then. I need the ID corrected to CL-88291, the contract resent to legal, and the three downstream reports regenerated and sent to finance. This needs to happen today, not next week, and not after you finish whatever else is currently ahead of it in your queue.

I also need to know why this wasn't caught the first two times it was flagged, but I don't need that explanation right now — I need the fix first. Once everything is corrected, send me the updated file names directly, not a summary, just the files. I'll check they're right myself.

Let's not let this sit another two weeks. Get it done today.
Hi Tomás, would you mind granting me access to the billing portal when you get a chance? Thanks so much for your help.

This is the fourth email I've sent about the deposit from the Ashworth event, and each time I get nothing back but silence. I'm done waiting on whatever internal process you people apparently don't have. Transfer the $1,200 to the account on file by end of day, or I'm disputing the charge with my bank and posting about this everywhere I can. Don't bother replying unless the money's already moved.

I know this is already the second time I've flagged the invoice error, which is frustrating, but I'd really appreciate it if you could take one more look — thank you for your patience with me on this.

Hi Renata, I'm really sorry to bring this up again, but I noticed the shipping address on order 4471 is still showing the old warehouse. I completely understand how busy things are right now, so please don't feel any pressure — whenever you're able to correct it would be wonderful. I can't thank you enough for all the patience you've shown me this month, truly.
I know refund requests must pile up endlessly on your end, so whatever time you can spare for mine, whenever that might be, would mean more than I can say.

Move the meeting to 2pm instead of 3. I have a hard stop at 4 today and won't get through the vendor agenda if we start late. Send the updated invite as soon as it's changed, and loop in the rest of the team yourself — I don't have time to forward it to everyone individually.

Hi Oskar,

I'm putting together the quarterly compliance packet and I need the updated vendor agreement template from your team. The version on the shared drive is from last January, and I think there have been at least two revisions since then based on the change log I saw in the project channel.

Could you send over the current version, or point me to where it's stored if it's been moved? I'd like to have it by Wednesday so I have time to review it before the packet goes to the audit team on Friday. If there's a reason the template hasn't been updated in the shared folder, that's fine, just let me know so I can note it in my summary.

I also wanted to check whether the liability clause changed in the last revision, since that's the section auditors usually ask about first. If you know offhand, a quick line in your reply would save me some digging, but if not, I can just read through the document myself once I have it.

Let me know if Wednesday doesn't work for you — I can probably push my own deadline by a day or two if needed. Otherwise, I'll plan around that timeline.

Thanks,
Nadia

Hi Mr. Donahue, I wanted to follow up on the deposit refund for the Lindqvist venue booking from last month. It's been about three weeks since the event, so I wanted to check on the status when you have a chance. Please send the refund to the account on file once it's processed. Thanks for your help with this.

Need three more days on the Kessler deliverable. The scope changed twice after the brief was sent, and the revised data set from your side only came in yesterday, so the original Friday deadline isn't realistic anymore.

Here's where things stand. The first two sections are done and reviewed. The third section depends entirely on the vendor numbers you're supposed to be sending, which still haven't shown up. Until those numbers are in, there's nothing more I can do on that part, regardless of the original date.

New deadline: next Monday, end of day. That gives me the weekend if the vendor numbers come in by Thursday, which they need to. If they're late again, Monday won't hold either, and I'm not the one who'll answer for that.

Send confirmation that Monday works. If it doesn't, say so today, not Sunday night, so I can plan around it instead of finding out at the last minute like last time.

I'll keep working on what I can in the meantime, but I'm not redoing the first two sections again if the scope changes a third time. Lock it in now or we're back here next week having the same conversation.

Marcus,

I'll give you credit for one thing — you're consistent. Every single deadline for the vendor compliance document gets missed by you, without fail, for three months running now. I get that things come up, sure, and I'm not trying to pile on, but at some point 'things come up' stops being an excuse and starts being a pattern, and I think we're well past that point.

I need the compliance document today. Not a draft, not 'almost there,' the finished version, formatted the way it was specified back in July, which somehow still hasn't happened despite being asked for it in writing at least six times.

I do appreciate that you've had a lot on your plate this quarter — genuinely, I'm not blind to that. But so has everyone else on this team, and somehow they've managed to hit their deadlines without turning it into a running joke. If this document isn't in my inbox by 5pm, I'm escalating to your manager and copying the compliance lead, and frankly I should have done that two months ago instead of continuing to be patient about something that clearly wasn't earning it.

Get it done. I'm done working around this.

The numbers on the Harrow report are off again — column D doesn't match the source file, same issue as last week. Redo the calculations and send the corrected version by noon. Double check against the source file this time before sending it back. I need this closed out before the client call at 1, no exceptions.
Friday, not Monday — that's the new date. Send whatever you have by end of day, finished or not.

Still haven't received the deposit refund from the Fenwick booking — it's been three weeks now, well past the ten-day window your policy states. Send it to the account on file today. I shouldn't have to follow up on this a second time. Confirm by email once it's done so I have it in writing.
I know I'm asking at an awful time, right before your conference deadline, and I feel terrible adding to your plate — but if you could still write the letter, I'd be more grateful than words can say.
Hi Farah, could you send over the updated budget template when you get a chance? Thanks so much, I really appreciate it.
Hi Professor Klein, would you be able to write a recommendation letter for my graduate application? The deadline is October 20th. Thanks.

Read through the draft you sent. The intro runs too long and the data section is missing a citation for the survey numbers you cited. Fix both of those and send the revised version back by tomorrow morning. Hold off on any other changes until those two things are sorted — I don't want to review a moving target.
Apparently I'm the last person on earth still working off the old deadline — could I get three extra days to catch up? Thanks for bearing with me.
You still haven't sent my recommendation letter and the deadline was yesterday — this is exactly the kind of carelessness I'd expect from you at this point.

Hi Mr. Castillo, I hope you're doing well. Would you mind taking a look at the attached draft and sharing your feedback sometime this week, whenever works for you? I know things are busy on your end, so there's no rush at all. Thank you so much for taking the time — I really value your input on this one.
I've asked three times now for access to the deployment console and nothing's happened — either grant it today or explain to me why this team can't handle something this basic.
Hi Elena, would you have a few minutes to look over my draft and share some feedback? I'd really appreciate your thoughts whenever it's convenient — thanks so much.

Dear Dr. Nkemelu, I hope this email finds you well. I'm applying to the environmental policy program at Ridgeview University, and I was wondering if you would be willing to write a recommendation letter on my behalf. The deadline is November 15th, and I'd be happy to send over my resume and personal statement if that would help. Thank you so much for considering it.

This is the third time I've had to chase you down about the deposit refund for the Brannigan wedding venue, and frankly I'm losing patience with how this is being handled. The money should have been back in our account two weeks ago per your own policy, yet somehow it's still 'being processed.' Either send it today or I'll be taking this up with your manager and leaving a review that reflects exactly how this was handled.

Hi Tobias, I noticed the totals on the March invoice don't match what's in the ledger — looks like the tax line might have been calculated twice. Could you take a look and send over a corrected version when you get a chance? I'd like to close this out before the end of the week if possible. Let me know if you have questions.
Last time you sent two lines on a forty-slide deck, so this time mark up every slide individually and have it back to me before end of day — I'm not doing another round after this.
I need three more days on the Pemberton deliverable, no discussion needed — the unrealistic timeline you set in the first place is the reason we're behind, not me.
Add me to the deployment server today. I need it before the 2pm release.
I still don't have access to the server after asking twice — figure it out or I'm escalating this to your boss today.
Need the recommendation letter by Friday. Send it straight to the admissions portal, not to me.

Hi Soraya, I know I already pushed this deadline back once, which I realize isn't great timing on my part. That said, could I get two more days on the compliance summary? The vendor data came in late again and I'd rather submit something accurate than rush it. Let me know if that works.
Oh, take your time fixing the invoice error — it's only been costing us money for two weeks, no big deal at all.

Hi Benedikt,

I wanted to check in about the deposit refund for the Solberg conference room booking from last month. According to the confirmation email I received at the time, refunds are typically processed within ten business days of the event, and it's now been just over three weeks since the event took place.

I don't think anything is necessarily wrong — these things sometimes just slip through the cracks when a lot of bookings are being processed at once — but I wanted to flag it in case it got missed. The original booking reference is SB-2291, and the deposit amount was 450 euros, paid by card at the time of booking.

Could you look into where things stand and let me know roughly when I should expect the refund to land? If there's additional paperwork needed on my end, I'm happy to send whatever's required, just let me know what that would be. I'd also appreciate it if you could confirm the refund will go back to the original card rather than requiring a new payment method on file, since that tripped me up with a different booking a while back.

If it's easier, I can also call the office directly this week instead of going back and forth by email — whatever's more convenient for your team. I just want to make sure this doesn't fall further behind schedule.

Thanks for looking into it.

Best,
Lena

Dear Professor Alberts, I'm so sorry to impose on your time, especially so close to finals week, but I was wondering if you might be willing to write a letter of recommendation for my scholarship application. I would completely understand if your schedule doesn't allow it. If you're able to help, I would be endlessly grateful and would happily provide anything that might make it easier, like my transcript or a summary of our work together. Thank you so much, either way, for even considering it.

Dear Mr. Castellanos,

I feel like I should just set up a recurring calendar reminder titled 'Ingrid asks for more time again,' because at this rate you probably have my name memorized for all the wrong reasons. I promise I'm not usually this person, though it's becoming harder to prove that with each passing quarter.

All jokes aside, I'm writing to ask, with as much humility as I can manage at this point, whether it might be possible to extend the deadline on the Castellanos merger summary by four more days. The additional due-diligence documents from the other side only arrived yesterday, and I want to make sure I do the analysis justice rather than rushing something incomplete just to hit the original date.

I know how much you've already accommodated me this year, and I genuinely don't take that for granted, even when my emails might suggest I'm developing a bad habit. If four days isn't workable, I completely understand, and I'll find a way to make the original deadline work rather than ask for anything further.

Whatever you decide, I want to say how grateful I am for your patience with me throughout this project. It has meant more than I think I've properly expressed, and I don't want that to get lost underneath my ongoing, slightly embarrassing tendency to ask for extra time.

Thank you again, truly, for even reading this far.

Warmly,
Ingrid Solano

Dear Mr. Okafor,

I want to start by saying I'm genuinely embarrassed to be writing this email, and I've rewritten it three times trying to find a way to bring this up that doesn't sound like I'm making excuses, because I'm not trying to.

I made an error in the shipment count I sent you last Tuesday for the Delacroix order — I listed 400 units when the correct number, confirmed against our warehouse records this morning, is actually 340. I know this kind of mistake can cause real problems on your end, especially if you've already adjusted your own inventory planning or communicated the higher number to your team, and I am so sorry for any trouble this may cause you.

Would it be possible for you to update your records to reflect the corrected count of 340 units? I completely understand if this creates complications, and I want you to know I'm available at any hour this week, including evenings, if it would help to talk through how to minimize the disruption on your side.

I also want to say, even though this email is about a mistake I made, how much I've valued working with you and your team over the past year. Your patience with me today, and honestly with our team in general, does not go unnoticed, and I am more grateful for it than this email probably conveys.

Thank you again for your understanding, and please don't hesitate to reach out if there's anything at all I can do to make this easier on your end.

With sincere apologies and gratitude,
Naledi Osei
Hi Dr. Sanderson, I'm applying to the Whitmore fellowship with a December 1st deadline — could you write a recommendation letter for me? Happy to send my CV if useful.
Your 'feedback' on my report was completely useless — two vague sentences after I waited a week for it. Next time either do it properly or don't bother.
I'm sorry to ask for more of your time, but would it be possible to grab fifteen minutes this week to go over the rollout plan? I'd be really grateful, whenever suits you best.

Hi Jonas, would you be available for a quick meeting sometime this week to go over the onboarding timeline? I'm free Tuesday afternoon or Thursday morning, but happy to work around your schedule. Please let me know what works, and thanks in advance for making time.
Got the draft, and the formatting's better this time — but the appendix is still missing. Send the complete version by noon, no more partial files.

Hi Rashid, could you set me up with access to the inventory system when you get a chance? I'll need it to run the month-end reports starting next week. Let me know if you need a manager approval or anything else from me to process the request. Thanks.
Hi Talia, are you free for a quick call this week to go over the budget? Let me know what time works.
The reference number on invoice 4471 is one digit off — could you correct it and send an updated copy?
The booking for October 14 was cancelled before the cutoff, so the $250 deposit needs to go back to the card on file this week.
The billing system needs read access enabled for my account before I can pull the September statements — can you set that up?
Could you update the shipping address on order 8823 to 14 Birch Lane — it's currently listed as Birch Street?

The lease agreement sent yesterday is missing page 3, which covers the renewal terms and the early termination clause. I need the complete version to file with the property office before their Wednesday cutoff. The copy on record at my end only goes up to page 2, so I can't tell if anything else was left out. Could you resend the full document with that page included?
The meeting notes from Tuesday don't include the budget figures that were discussed — please send an updated version with those numbers added.

I'm applying for the Hartwell research grant, which has a submission deadline of November 3rd. The application requires one letter of recommendation from a prior supervisor, submitted directly through the grant portal. Would you be able to write one on my behalf? The letter should speak to my research methodology coursework and the lab work I completed last spring.

The catering order for the Whitfield office event was cancelled two weeks ago, and the $180 deposit hasn't been returned yet. The confirmation email listed a five-business-day turnaround for refunds after cancellation, and that window closed last Friday. The charge was made on the office corporate card ending in 4417. Could you check on the status and process it to the original payment method?

The quarterly summary you sent lists the Denholm account under the Northeast region instead of Midwest, which throws off the regional totals on page two. The correction needs to go out before the report is forwarded to the board on Friday morning. The Midwest total should read $342,000 once the account is moved over. Please update the figure and send the corrected file.
